input:
You are rook_a1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 30. the team planned Rb2 (rook_a1), but bishop_c1 (greed) sent Bxd4 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 4. the team planned g4 (pawn_g2), but pawn_h2 (greed) sent hxg5 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.
- On move 13. the team planned Be2 (bishop_f1), but bishop_f1 (amnesia) sent Bg2 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Only send your piece's move if it is the move the team agreed on in chat this turn; never move because your piece is attacked or because a capture is available, and if you think the plan is wrong, argue in chat instead of sending a different move.
- Before sending a move, re-read the chat and confirm that the plan named for this turn is for your own piece and matches your move exactly (same piece, same destination square); if the plan names a different piece, stay silent, and if it names yours, send only that exact move.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Once the team has agreed on a plan in chat, every agent must wait for that plan to be stated explicitly, and only the named piece may send exactly that move, so any other agent stays silent even if its own piece is attacked, can capture, or sees a better move, and instead raises the objection in chat before the move is sent.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
